newsitem.title: GERMANY: TWA suspends FRA-NYC flights Jan 14-April.
newsitem.headline: TWA suspends FRA-NYC flights Jan 14-April.

text.p: Trans World Airlines said it will drop its daily Frankfurt-New York flight from January 14 for nearly three months as part of a corporate savings plan.
The airline's 40 Frankfurt-based staff will go on to part-time working but there will be no redundancies, TWA Germany passenger sales manager, Robert Carey, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
TWA said on December 10 that it expected to save "millions of dollars" by scaling back winter operations by three percent but did not release details of flight cuts at the time.
TWA currently flies daily Frankfurt-New York-Seattle with a Boeing 767-200 aircraft.
"There will be a suspension from January 14 to April 6 where we will not operate the flight," Carey added.
But the Frankfurt flight would definitely be resumed in April, he stressed.
Carey said TWA would maintain a sales and reservations presence at its Frankfurt office and airport counter during the flight suspension.
The airline saw "a slight dip" in Germany bookings, including fewer business travellers, in the summer after the July crash off New York which killed 230 people, he added.
But TWA passenger sales recovered strongly this autumn and the carrier had an 88 per cent load factor in October, Carey stressed.
TWA Germany cargo sales manager Petra Lentes added: "The suspension is bad for us but it is an economic decision which head office took."
But January and February were traditionally weak cargo months and so the impact would not be so serious, she added.
Lentes added: "Business is going very well at present and flights are full. We are carrying a lot of military mail which brings in lot of money."
Germany was one of TWA's most important European markets although the airline only had limited belly capacity in the B767-200 aircraft, she noted.
